summary.tldr: Requires a national framework on sports betting advertising, plus reports to Parliament and a CRTC review of related rules.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Canadian Heritage to develop a national framework for sports betting ads, including ways to limit ad use, number, scope, location, and the use of celebrities and athletes.
Requires the framework to include measures for research, information-sharing, and national standards for preventing and diagnosing harmful gambling and addiction, and for supporting affected people.
Requires the minister to consult federal ministers, provinces and territories, Indigenous communities, regulators, and other stakeholders while developing the framework.
Requires the minister to table a report with the framework and an implementation plan within one year, then a second report within five years on what was carried out and what was not.
Requires the CRTC to review its regulations and policies on sports betting advertising and report its conclusions and recommendations to the minister within one year of royal assent.
